new_jobs.description:
Overview

Location(s): United States

Practice/Department: Business Operations

Work Environment: Remote

Compensation: $135,000-$150,000 annually*

Dudek’s journey began in 1980 with a vision to serve Southern California’s water and wastewater agencies.

Today, we are a 100% employee-owned firm supporting clients nationwide and delivering projects that improve and protect the built and natural environments of communities throughout the United States. Our work has been recognized by leading industry organizations , and we’ve been honored with multiple national Top Workplace Awards.

Our employee-owners are unified by a singular commitment to supporting projects that address key societal issues, such as the transition to renewable energy, infrastructure hardening and repair, environmental protection, and community resilience.

Learn more about our award-winning culture
, the benefits and perks
of being a Dudekian , and the projects
you will have the opportunity to shape.

Position Overview

Who You Are

As an employee-owner
, you embrace accountability, working safely, and collaboration while thinking resourcefully and independently.

Like all Dudekians , you are curious and solution-oriented
, with the ability to adapt quickly to changes and approach challenges with a spirit of innovation
.

How You’ll Make An Impact

Dudek is looking for a Business Operations Manager (HRIS) to provide leadership and strategic oversight for Dudek’s HR technology ecosystem, with primary responsibility for Dayforce HCM and the systems, data, integrations, and processes that support the employee lifecycle. This role will ensure HR technology is reliable, secure, well governed, scalable, and aligned with Dudek’s evolving business and workforce needs.

Working closely with Human Resources, Finance, Payroll, Benefits, IT, and other key stakeholders, the Business Operations Manager (HRIS) will serve as a critical connector between business processes and technology. The role will lead HRIS strategy and optimization, data and integration governance, system implementations and enhancements, and cross functional initiatives involving interconnected HR, ERP, financial, and enterprise systems.

The Business Operations Manager (HRIS) will also lead the HRIS team and support model, establish strong system governance and controls, and help Dudek maximize the value of its HR technology investments while supporting an effective employee and manager experience.

Candidates must be available to work during Pacific Time business hours (8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. PT).

Duties And Responsibilities

HRIS Strategy & Platform Leadership

Leads the administration, configuration, optimization, and ongoing evolution of Dayforce HCM and Dudek’s broader HR technology ecosystem.
Develops and maintains an HRIS roadmap aligned with HR priorities, enterprise technology initiatives, business growth, and evolving operational needs.
Evaluates opportunities to simplify, automate, and improve HR processes through technology while balancing business requirements, user experience, system capabilities, risk, and long-term scalability.
Maintains a strong understanding of HR technology trends, platform capabilities, and vendor roadmaps and recommends opportunities to improve Dudek’s HR technology environment.
Establishes standards and governance for HR system configuration, enhancements, testing, releases, documentation, and change management.

Enterprise Systems & Integration Leadership

Serves as the HRIS functional lead for major enterprise technology transformations, representing HR systems, employee data, integrations, controls, and workforce process requirements in cross-functional design and implementation decisions.
Serves as a key HRIS partner in the design, implementation, and ongoing optimization of integrations between Dayforce, Deltek Vantagepoint, iCIMS, and other enterprise platforms.
Partners closely with Finance and other business leaders on ERP initiatives involving employee, organizational, labor, payroll, time, project, or other shared data and processes.
Collaborates with IT, Information Security, system owners, vendors, and implementation partners to establish effective integration architecture, data flows, system dependencies, controls, and support models.
Leads HRIS participation in enterprise system implementations, upgrades, integrations, testing, data conversions, and other major technology initiatives.
Identifies and resolves complex cross-system issues, including determining root cause, coordinating stakeholders, and driving solutions through completion.
Assesses downstream impacts of system and process changes to help ensure changes made in one platform do not adversely affect interconnected systems or business processes.

Data Governance, Security & Controls

Oversees the integrity, consistency, and appropriate use of HR and employee data across HR systems and system integrations.
Establishes and maintains HRIS data governance practices, including data ownership, definitions, validation, reconciliation, and documentation, in alignment with the governance and control standards established by IT.
Administers HR system access, role-based security, and data protection practices in accordance with the security standards and controls established by IT and Information Security.
Partners with IT and Information Security to support audits, access reviews, compliance activities, and other control requirements related to HR systems and employee data.
Maintains documentation of system configurations, integrations, data flows, procedures, control activities, and key system decisions.
Monitors system and integration performance and proactively addresses risks that could affect data integrity, payroll, financial reporting, employee processes, or business operations.

HR Technology Operations & Support

Leads HR technology support through Dudek’s Business Operations service model, ensuring requests and issues are effectively prioritized, routed, resolved, and communicated.
Builds and manages the HRIS support structure in Freshservice, including intake, categorization, forms, workflows, service levels, escalation paths, and knowledge resources.
Supports iCIMS (Applicant Tracking System) and other people-related technology, including system administration, integrations, configuration, and ongoing optimization as appropriate.
Leads the HR Service Family workspace design and adoption.
Partners with Human Resources, Payroll, Benefits, Finance, and other stakeholders to translate business and process needs into sustainable system solutions.
Establishes processes for identifying recurring issues, analyzing root causes, and implementing longer-term solutions rather than relying on manual workarounds.
Develops and maintains HRIS documentation, procedures, knowledge resources, and training materials that support users and promote consistent system practices.

Projects, Optimization & Change

Leads and participates in complex HRIS and cross-functional technology projects from requirements gathering and solution design through testing, implementation, stabilization, and ongoing support.
Establishes project plans, priorities, requirements, testing strategies, risks, dependencies, and stakeholder responsibilities for HR technology initiatives.
Coordinates user acceptance testing and validates that solutions meet business requirements before implementation.
Partners with stakeholders to support effective communication, training, rollout, and adoption of new systems, enhancements, and processes.
Balances immediate operational needs with long-term system architecture and business objectives when evaluating solutions and priorities.

Reporting & Analytics

Partners with HR and business leaders to improve access to accurate, meaningful, and appropriately governed workforce information.
Oversees HRIS reporting capabilities, data extracts, interfaces, and recurring reporting processes.
Supports the development of reporting and analytics solutions that improve workforce planning, decision-making, operational visibility, and data consistency.
Helps establish common workforce data definitions and sources of truth across HR, Finance, and other functions.

Vendor & Partner Management

Serves as a key point of contact for HR technology vendors and implementation partners.
Manages vendor escalations, system issues, enhancement discussions, release planning, and technical coordination as appropriate.
Evaluates vendor capabilities and proposed solutions to ensure they align with Dudek’s requirements, security expectations, technology environment, and long-term strategy.

Team Leadership

Leads, develops, and supports HRIS team members, including Business Operations Analysts (HRIS) and other assigned resources, and manages onboarding and the support queue.
Establishes priorities and distributes work across system administration, projects, enhancements, reporting, integrations, and user support.
Builds team capability through coaching, documentation, cross-training, and knowledge transfer to reduce key-person dependencies and strengthen service continuity.
Promotes a collaborative, service-oriented approach while establishing clear accountability for system quality, responsiveness, and results.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience: 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in HRIS, HR technology, enterprise systems, or related systems roles, including recent experience with Dayforce or a comparable enterprise HCM platform (e.g., UKG, Oracle, Workday, SAP)
Demonstrated experience leading complex system implementations, integrations, enhancements, or transformation initiatives involving multiple business functions.
Experience working with integrations between HR, payroll, ERP, financial, recruiting, or other enterprise systems.
Strong understanding of HR data governance, system security, role-based access, integrations, testing, change management, and system controls.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex business requirements into effective, scalable system solutions.
Demonstrated experience working with technical and nontechnical stakeholders and communicating complex system concepts in clear business terms.
Experience leading or developing HRIS professionals and managing competing operational and project priorities.
Ability to work Pacific Time Zone business hours is required.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and partner effectively across departments in remote, hybrid, and office environments while maintaining productivity, accountability, and responsiveness.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Dayforce HCM, Deltek Vantagepoint, iCIMS, Freshservice, or comparable platforms.
Experience supporting HRIS/ERP integrations or enterprise technology transformation initiatives.
Experience partnering with Finance, IT, Information Security, Payroll, and Human Resources in a complex system environment.
Experience with system governance, data governance, audit controls, integration management, and vendor management.
Certification(s): SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, HRIP, Dayforce, project management, or other relevant HR, technology, or systems certification.

Compensation:
$135,000-$150,000 annually*

Final agreed-upon compensation will be based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, an individual’s related experience, education, certifications, skills, and work location. Successful candidates must pass a pre-employment drug test and background check prior to beginning employment.

This job operates in a remote or office-based environment and this role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, printers, etc.

new_jobs.title: AI Business Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
The AI Business Intelligence Analyst - HR & Talent Acquisition converts workforce, candidate, recruitment, and recruiter-performance data into trusted dashboards, automated reporting, operational intelligence, and business recommendations. The role owns the full reporting lifecycle: requirements gathering, data validation, modeling, visualization, AI-assisted analysis, insight development, and executive communication.

The analyst partners with Talent Acquisition, HR, Operations, Workforce Management, Finance, Technology, and site leadership to identify hiring risks early, improve funnel conversion, strengthen recruiter effectiveness, reduce manual reporting, and support evidence-based workforce decisions

Primary Business Outcomes

Create one trusted source of truth for Talent Acquisition and priority HR performance measures.
Give leaders early visibility into class-fill risk, funnel leakage, candidate fallout, recruiter capacity, and workforce demand.
Shorten the time from data extraction to business action through automation and AI-assisted analysis.
Improve the quality and consistency of operational reviews, recruiter coaching, workforce planning, and executive decisions.
Establish responsible, human-reviewed use of generative AI across HR and recruiting analytics.

Key Accountabilities

1. HR and Talent Acquisition Business Intelligence

Design, build, test, publish, and maintain HR and recruiting dashboards, scorecards, exception reports, and business-review packs.
Develop end-to-end recruitment funnel reporting covering demand, requisitions, leads, contact attempts, screening, assessments, interviews, offers, requirements completion, onboarding, Day 1 attendance, and early-tenure outcomes.
Build workforce and people dashboards covering headcount, movement, attrition, absenteeism, retention, staffing gaps, productivity, and other approved HR measures.
Create data models, DAX measures, drill-through views, cohort analyses, segmentation, trend views, and recruiter or site-level performance cuts.
Translate HR and TA operating questions into clear business requirements, KPI definitions, calculation rules, report logic, and visualization designs.
Document data sources, metric owners, assumptions, refresh schedules, dependencies, filters, and approved sources of truth.

2. Recruiting Insights and Decision Support

Identify class-fill risk, lead aging, funnel bottlenecks, conversion gaps, candidate fallout, no-show patterns, recruiter workload imbalance, and sourcing-channel performance.
Explain what happened, why it happened, what is likely to happen next, and which intervention should be prioritized.
Develop hiring forecasts, funnel survival models, capacity scenarios, source-mix analysis, recruiter productivity views, and location or talent-pool intelligence.
Connect recruiting outcomes to operational demand, training readiness, start-date requirements, early-tenure retention, and approved quality-of-hire indicators.
Produce concise insight narratives for daily stand-ups, weekly operating reviews, executive reviews, workforce planning, and client discussions.
Convert findings into recommended actions with owners, deadlines, expected impact, and follow-through measures.

3. AI Prompting and Conversational Analytics

Create reusable prompts and AI-assisted workflows that summarize recruiting performance, identify patterns, classify root causes, and draft evidence-based report commentary.
Analyze approved candidate and recruiter interaction data to identify call behaviors, candidate objections, unresolved questions, process misses, and coaching opportunities.
Develop prompt templates, evaluation rubrics, test cases, and human-in-the-loop review controls for recurring HR and TA use cases.
Maintain a governed prompt library that documents approved inputs, intended use, expected output, limitations, validation steps, ownership, and version history.
Test AI outputs for factual accuracy, unsupported conclusions, bias, privacy exposure, inconsistent logic, and sensitivity to prompt wording or incomplete data.
Ensure AI supports not replaces recruiter, HR, and leadership judgment. The role does not authorize fully automated employment decisions.

4. Reporting and Workflow Automation

Automate recurring data preparation, report refresh, commentary generation, distribution, exception alerts, and approved follow-up workflows.
Integrate or reconcile data from ATS/CRM, HRIS, assessment, telephony, quality, workforce, finance, onboarding, and learning systems.
Reduce spreadsheet dependency, duplicate reporting, manual consolidation, and inconsistent calculations while preserving clear control points.
Develop proactive alerts that identify at-risk candidates, aging requisitions, unfilled classes, unusual conversion shifts, missing requirements, or data-quality failures.
Track hours saved, defects reduced, cycle-time improvement, user adoption, and business value generated by automation.

Data Quality, Privacy, and Responsible AI

Validate source completeness, reconcile conflicting figures, investigate anomalies, and prevent unverified information from reaching decision-makers.
Maintain an HR and TA metric dictionary with definitions, inclusions, exclusions, calculation rules, ownership, and approved sources.
Protect employee, candidate, client, compensation, performance, and personally identifiable information through appropriate access, minimization, and retention controls.
Use only approved AI tools and approved data inputs; do not place confidential HR or candidate data into unapproved public AI services.
Clearly distinguish verified findings, analytical estimates, AI-generated hypotheses, and areas where the evidence is insufficient.
Partner with Privacy, Security, Legal, HR, and Technology teams on governance, access, auditability, and appropriate use of analytics in employment decisions.

Stakeholder Partnership and Enablement

Partner with TA leaders, recruiters, sourcers, onboarding teams, HRBPs, Operations, Workforce Management, Finance, Training, and technology owners.
Facilitate requirements sessions and challenge requests that produce activity reports without a clear decision or business use.
Train leaders and end users to interpret dashboards, use metric definitions correctly, ask stronger analytical questions, and apply approved AI workflows safely.
Monitor report adoption and stakeholder feedback; improve high-value products and retire low-value or duplicative reports.
Present findings confidently to operational and executive audiences, including uncomfortable findings that the evidence supports.

Core Deliverables

TA command-center dashboard covering demand, funnel, conversion, class-fill confidence, source performance, aging, and risk.
Daily and weekly exception reporting for leads, assessments, interviews, offers, requirements, onboarding, and Day 1 attendance.
Recruiter and team performance scorecards with productivity, conversion, quality, aging, adherence, and coaching context.
Candidate-call analytics covering behaviors, objections, unresolved concerns, process adherence, and coaching opportunities.
HR workforce dashboards for approved headcount, attrition, movement, attendance, retention, capacity, and workforce-planning measures.
Executive insight summaries with verified findings, implications, recommended actions, owners, and measured impact.
AI prompt library, evaluation tests, control documentation, and human-review procedures.
Metric dictionary, data lineage notes, report inventory, refresh calendar, access matrix, and reporting roadmap.

Required Qualifications

Approximately two or more years of relevant experience in BI development, people analytics, recruiting analytics, reporting, operations analytics, or a closely related discipline. Equivalent demonstrated capability may substitute for tenure.
A portfolio showing dashboards, data models, automated reports, or analytical products built personally not merely reports consumed or coordinated.
Demonstrated capability in SQL, spreadsheets, data preparation, and at least one enterprise BI platform.
Practical experience using generative AI for structured analysis, prompting, workflow acceleration, text analysis, or report development.
Working knowledge of recruitment funnels, HR data, operational KPIs, data privacy, and the sensitivity of employment-related information.
Strong business writing, visualization, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain findings to nontechnical leaders.
Evidence of analytical judgment, data skepticism, quality control, ownership, and comfort working with incomplete or conflicting requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience supporting Talent Acquisition, HR, workforce operations, high-volume hiring, BPO, shared services, or multi-site operations.
Experience combining ATS/CRM, telephony, assessment, HRIS, onboarding, and operational data into one reporting model.
Experience automating recurring reports or analytical workflows through low-code tools, APIs, SQL, or Python.
Exposure to call or text analytics, forecasting, predictive analytics, natural-language-to-SQL, retrieval-based AI, or AI agents.
Relevant certification in Power BI, Tableau, analytics, cloud platforms, process improvement, data engineering, HR analytics, or responsible AI. Certifications do not replace a work sample.
Bachelor's degree in analytics, information systems, computer science, statistics, economics, industrial engineering, psychology, human resources, business, or a related field; equivalent practical experience is acceptable.

Archer
is collaborating with Vanguard
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.

Technology is the enabling force powering Vanguard’s client experience, investment products, and advice. As technology continues to evolve, so does the need for leaders who can identify, assess, and mitigate risk across complex systems. Vanguard’s Technology Leadership Program (TLP) is designed to develop the next generation of IT leaders through hands-on experience, collaboration, and rotational learning. Through three unique rotations, you will build technical expertise in cybersecurity and risk while developing the leadership skills needed to protect Vanguard and its clients.

Protect What Matters Most

At Vanguard, we’re committed to doing what’s right for our clients - and that starts with protecting their data, assets, and trust. As part of the Technology Leadership Program in the Risk & Security Analyst track, you’ll help identify, assess, and mitigate risks that impact Vanguard’s systems, operations, and clients. Your work will contribute to safeguarding Vanguard against evolving cybersecurity threats and operational risks. Through real-world assignments and collaboration across technology and business teams, you’ll gain exposure to how risk and security practices enable Vanguard to deliver secure, reliable services to investors.

Are you a self-starter who thrives on solving complex challenges and thinking critically about risk? Join a team where innovation is driven by purpose. You’ll work alongside cybersecurity, technology, and business partners to analyze threats, strengthen controls, and support risk-informed decision-making. Through technical capstones, hackathons, and hands-on projects, you’ll build both your analytical skillset and your ability to collaborate, influence, and lead.

The Technology Leadership Program is a two-year rotational development experience designed for graduating students ready to begin their careers in technology. Participants complete three eight-month rotations across Risk & Security-focused teams, gaining exposure to different areas such as cybersecurity operations, threat intelligence, risk management, and identity & access management - while increasing ownership, responsibility, and leadership capability over time.

In This Program, You Will

Support efforts to identify, assess, and mitigate cybersecurity and operational risks
Analyze potential threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios across systems and processes
Contribute to reporting, dashboards, or insights that support risk-informed decision-making
Partner with security, technology, and business teams to strengthen controls and processes
Gain hands-on experience in risk management, cybersecurity frameworks, and digital ethics
Apply Agile methodologies to support risk and security initiatives in a dynamic environment
Take ownership of projects and contribute to delivering meaningful outcomes
Collaborate across teams, share insights, and drive solutions in a supportive environment
Build a network with program managers, alumni, senior leaders, and peers
Meet regularly with your department manager and program manager to receive personalized coaching and mentorship

What It Takes

Bachelor's or Master's degree with a concentration in computer science, computer engineering, IST, IT, CIS, Security, Risk, Cybersecurity or related technical/engineering subject matter required
Strong interest in cybersecurity, threat analysis, risk management, or fraud prevention
Demonstrated leadership potential, initiative, and ability to take ownership of work
Strong analytical, communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative, team-oriented environment
Cumulative GPA of 3.2 or higher preferred

Special Factors

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.
This position will begin in 2027. December 2026 and Spring 2027 grads are encouraged to apply.

Benefits

Our Total Rewards package reflects our commitment to you and your family’s well-being – both for today and for the future. We invest in your financial, physical, and personal success with best-in-class benefits through:

Pay for performance, including annual performance bonuses, merit increases, and an annual Partnership bonus.
Industry-leading retirement savings plans:
401(k) contribution 55% above the national average.
Quarterly 401(k) contribution of 10% of your eligible pay.
At least 18 paid days off, plus 10 federal holidays.
77% of your medical costs are covered, compared to 68% by other financial services companies.
Unparalleled Health Savings Account (HSA) seed and match – 5x the amount as other contributing employers.
A $1500 FlexFund annual stipend for personally meaningful conveniences – 3x the average amount offered by other employers.
Top-tier programs for your emotional and mental health:
Access to 2x more coaching and therapy sessions compared to other employers.
A caregiving concierge program, something only one in five employers offer.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

new_jobs.description:

MANTECH
seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Operations Research Analyst
to join our team in Tampa, FL
.

The Operations Research Analyst will leverage their strong technical background and knowledge to introduce quantitative and qualitative analysis to the decision-making processes by developing and applying probability models, statistical inference, simulations, optimizations, and economic models.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Using statistical analysis, simulations, predictive modeling, and other methods to analyze information in support of USSOCOM processes and decision-making.
Employing analytic and operational design methodologies to frame complex problems to help senior military and civilian leaders develop solutions and strategies.
Providing analytical support involving mathematical modeling, statistical methods, and operational mathematics techniques such as game theory and probability theory.
Transforming raw data into information and recommendations by gathering and identifying data variables within models using qualitative and quantitative tests.
Researching, designing, and implementing algorithms to solve complex problems while programming in R, Python, or similar analytical languages.
Using frameworks such as Spark and Hadoop to conduct large-scale data processing and creating data visualizations using Tableau, Power BI, or R Shiny.
Applying systems thinking and value-focused thinking to facilitate clear force employment and resourcing decisions across tactical, operational, and strategic levels.
Conducting and supporting studies, war-games, and modeling efforts to assist decision makers in framing and solving complex problems.
Refining and developing methods to display data and findings to facilitate senior leaders quickly grasping key findings from analytic work.

Minimum Qualifications

Master's Degree in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Industrial Engineering, Statistics, or related math discipline; OR a Bachelor's Degree in the same fields with 4 years of experience in Operations Research and Analysis in military matters.
5+ years of experience preparing written products for senior leader use and communicating at all levels in a highly professional manner.
Experience conducting both quantitative and qualitative analysis and applying scientific methodology to discover and frame relevant problems.
Proficiency in programming using R or Python (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas) and using data visualization tools.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with the Sponsor’s primary cyber risk and compliance automation tools.

Clearance Requirements

An active Secret clearance is required with the ability to obtain and maintain TS/SCI

Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50%.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst (AIA Investment Management)
new_jobs.description:
Start building a career with purpose.

At AIA, your perspective, curiosity and ideas can contribute to our Purpose of helping millions of people live Healthier, Longer, Better Lives. Across our diverse markets, you will learn through meaningful work, collaborate with experienced colleagues and build practical skills as you turn fresh ideas into positive outcomes and a more sustainable future for our customers and communities.

Join us to explore new possibilities, grow through real experiences and start making an impact across Asia.

About The Role

Join us as Data Analyst at AIA Investment Management!

At AIA Investment Management, we believe in creating long-term value for our clients and communities. We are seeking a Data Analyst to join our Data Science and Analytics team. In this role, you will serve as a central coordinator for data sourcing and management, working closely with internal stakeholders and data providers to collect, collate, cleanse, transform, and validate data for analytical and reporting purposes. You will be responsible for ensuring the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of data, conducting data quality checks, and supporting the timely delivery of high-quality data used in investment analysis, reporting, and decision-making processes. Partnering across functions, you will help strengthen data governance and quality standards, while building deep expertise in investment data and contributing to the development of the team's analytics capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

As part of our high-performing team, you will be responsible for:

Data Sourcing and Coordination
Coordinate with business users, data owners, technology teams, and external data providers to obtain data required for analysis and reporting.
Follow up on data requests, clarify data requirements, track delivery status, and highlight delays or gaps promptly.
Identify suitable data sources and document source ownership, file locations, formats, refresh frequency, and key business definitions.
Data Collation and Preparation
Collect and consolidate data from multiple sources, including spreadsheets, documents, emails, system extracts, and other structured or unstructured inputs.
Organise and standardise data into consistent templates and structures that can be used by the Data Science and Analytics team.
Convert unstructured or semi-structured information into structured datasets while preserving source details and traceability.
Data Cleaning and ETL
Perform routine data extraction, transformation, and loading activities using tools such as Excel, SQL, or Python.
Clean and standardise data by resolving formatting differences, duplicates, missing values, inconsistent labels, and other common data issues.
Prepare repeatable data processing steps and maintain simple scripts, queries, templates, or workflows under guidance from senior team members.
Data Quality Checks and Issue Resolution
Perform completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, and reconciliation checks before data is used for analysis or reporting.
Investigate data exceptions, compare results with source records, and work with data owners to resolve identified issues.
Maintain data quality checklists, issue logs, validation evidence, and clear records of corrections or assumptions.
Documentation and Team Support
Maintain data dictionaries, process notes, file inventories, data lineage records, and operating instructions.
Provide timely progress updates, communicate issues clearly, and support knowledge sharing within the team.
Learn new data tools, business concepts, and working methods as required, and apply feedback to improve the quality and efficiency of work.

Minimum Requirements

We are looking for professionals who possess:

Bachelor's degree or Polytechnic diploma in Data Science, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, or a related discipline, with relevant internship, academic project, or practical experience involving data sourcing, data preparation, ETL, and/or data quality management.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; exposure to SQL, Python, Power Query, or similar data preparation tools would be advantageous.
Basic understanding of data cleansing, data transformation, ETL processes, and data quality checks, coupled with strong analytical and problem-solving skills to investigate discrepancies and validate information against source data.
Strong attention to detail, with the ability to work accurately with large datasets, maintain proper documentation, follow established processes, and meet agreed timelines.
Good written and verbal communication skills, with the professionalism and confidence to engage data owners and stakeholders effectively and work collaboratively across teams.
A proactive learning mindset, with the willingness to learn new tools, business concepts, and data processes.
Exposure to investment management, financial data, reporting, cloud data platforms, or data visualisation tools would be advantageous but is not required.

Believe in better with AIA. If you work at AIA, you play an important part in this movement. Which is why we give you every opportunity to learn, grow and shape your career - your way!

Build a career with us as we help our customers and the community live Healthier, Longer, Better Lives.

You must provide all requested information, including Personal Data, to be considered for this career opportunity. Failure to provide such information may influence the processing and outcome of your application. You are responsible for ensuring that the information you submit is accurate and up-to-date.

ABOUT AIA

For over a century, AIA has served the ever-changing needs of our customers across Asia-Pacific. Our Purpose to help millions of people live Healthier, Longer, Better Lives is at the heart of everything we do.

As pioneering innovators, we’re now transforming AIA to be faster, simpler and more connected to create better solutions and impactful experiences for our customers and communities. AIA encourages and enables our people to act with clarity, courage and humanity in service of our Purpose.

JOIN US

At AIA, we believe in empowering every one of our people to find their 'better' - in the work they do, the career they build, the life they live and the difference they make. Whether it’s investing better wellbeing, inspiring better learning, building better relationships, or making a better impact on customers, a career at AIA will challenge you to find new ways to pursue your ‘better’.

AIA is committed to building a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive workforce for all employees to thrive in. Join us if you believe in creating a better tomorrow!

Affinity is seeking an experienced InfraSec Project Manager to lead complex, enterprise-scale technology projects within a strategic Project Management Office.

Lead end-to-end delivery of large-scale, high-impact enterprise technology projects, with a strong focus on infrastructure, security, and platform integration
Drive environment build-outs, technical integrations, and migration activities to support the transition from a legacy core system to a modern platform ecosystem
Define and refine project scope, success metrics, deliverables, and business outcomes aligned to strategic goals and regulatory requirements
Develop and manage integrated delivery plans including resource allocation, financials, schedules, risk frameworks, and quality controls
Provide strategic leadership across complex technical domains including integration patterns, networking, authentication, IAM, cloud infrastructure, and data migration
Act as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders, ensuring alignment, sponsorship, and informed decision-making across the program lifecycle
Establish and enforce strong governance practices, including risk/issue management, change control, and compliance oversight
Lead cross-functional teams spanning engineering, infrastructure, security, vendors, and business stakeholders
Manage third-party vendors and platform partners, ensuring adherence to contractual deliverables, timelines, and service expectations
Deliver executive-level reporting on project health, risks, dependencies, and overall program status
Drive organizational change management strategies to enable successful adoption of new platforms, tools, and workflows
Partner with business and technical leaders to assess change impacts and deliver communications, training, and readiness plans
Ensure technology integration strategies align with enterprise architecture and security principles
Conduct post-implementation reviews to capture lessons learned and continuously improve delivery practices

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline; advanced degree is an asset
10+ years of progressive project management experience delivering complex, enterprise-scale technology initiatives
Proven experience leading large-scale platform transformations, system migrations, or core technology modernization programs
Strong technical project management background with demonstrated experience in infrastructure and security (infrasec) domains
Hands-on experience managing integration-heavy programs involving APIs, middleware, and enterprise data flows
Strong knowledge in key technical domains including networking, authentication, identity & access management (IAM), cloud infrastructure, and data migration
Demonstrated ability to deliver projects using both Waterfall and Agile methodologies in complex, regulated environments
PMP certification preferred; additional certifications such as SAFe, PRINCE2, or PMI-ACP are considered strong assets
Experience with organizational change management frameworks (e.g., Prosci) highly preferred
Expert knowledge of project governance, enterprise risk management, and compliance practices
Strong proficiency with Jira and Confluence
Experience operating within IT service management frameworks (e.g., ITIL) including change and incident management
Background in financial services or similarly regulated industries strongly preferred
Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with experience influencing senior and executive leadership
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and strategic thinking capabilities with a results-driven mindset

Top Skills Necessary

8+ years of enterprise project management experience delivering large-scale, technically complex transformation projects (e.g., platform migration, core system replacement).
5+ years of technical PM expertise in infrastructure and security domains, including IAM, cloud environments, authentication, or network integrations.
Executive stakeholder engagement and change leadership, including OCM strategy execution across enterprise-wide technology change

new_jobs.description:
What You'll Do

If you're someone who enjoys detailed financial work, problem-solving and partnering with people across teams, this is an opportunity to build your investment operations experience in a global environment.

As an Investment Operations Analyst
, you'll support the lifecycle of investments with an emphasis on collateral management. You'll work with internal teams and external partners, including brokers and custodians, to reconcile information, support margin activity, resolve discrepancies and help keep transactions moving accurately and on time.

This opportunity can be a strong fit for an early-career candidate with a finance-related degree as well as someone who already has exposure to investment or mutual fund operations. Previous investment operations experience is preferred, not required. The hiring leader confirmed that candidates entering the profession with a relevant degree can be considered.

What You'll Do

Independently execute routine and intermediate investment operations transactions while identifying and resolving issues according to established procedures.
Support collateral management activities involving derivatives, brokers and custodians, including reconciling market and derivative values and supporting margin-related transactions.
Support incoming and outgoing collateral activity, including applicable wire activity, and facilitate the booking of applicable transactions into accounting systems.
Establish securities, compliance rules, accounts, and reports that help support trading, reconciliation, settlement, and client reporting processes.
Investigate and resolve client-data issues, trade and reconciliation breaks, and compliance-related exceptions, escalating more complex matters when appropriate.
Prepare reporting and maintain controls consistent with established policies and client needs.
Collaborate with operations staff, legal, relationship management, technology teams, banks, brokers, custodians, portfolio managers, and traders to gather information and resolve issues.
Continue developing your understanding of investment products, procedures, and client needs through research, learning opportunities and ongoing investment activities.
Contribute to projects, process reviews and system enhancements supporting global investment initiatives.
Perform other job-related duties and special projects as needed.

Who You Are

You have a bachelor's degree, or equivalent, in accounting, finance, economics or business that has prepared you for success in an investment operations environment.
You bring 0+ years of investment/mutual fund operations or related experience.
You are highly detail-oriented and understand that accuracy matters.
You have strong analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, time-management and communication skills.
You communicate effectively and collaborate comfortably with different internal and external partners.
You can prioritize competing responsibilities, work under deadline pressure, and adjust when business needs change.
You can produce accurate and timely work with limited supervision.
You bring a client-service mindset to your work.

Experience And Knowledge That Could Help You Stand Out

Previous investment or mutual fund operations experience
Exposure to collateral management or collateral terminology
Experience with wire activity
Knowledge of financial-services and investment terminology
Experience working with Eagle for accounting and Excel for reconciliations or macros

Success in the role

Someone who thrives here will combine precision with adaptability. You'll be comfortable digging into discrepancies, communicating with multiple parties, following established controls, and recognizing when an issue needs to be escalated rather than handled independently.

new_jobs.title: Director, Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Program Manager based in the United States.

The Director, Program Manager will provide strategic leadership across a portfolio of technology programs, driving organizational performance, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. You will oversee and mentor a group of Program Managers while ensuring alignment between program objectives and broader business priorities. Working closely with customers and technical teams, you will identify opportunities, shape solutions, and strengthen long-term partnerships. You will also guide strategic and tactical planning, improve program management practices, and foster a culture of collaboration and servant leadership. The role combines executive-level oversight with active customer engagement and business development responsibilities. You will join a technically driven environment focused on delivering secure, reliable communication solutions while supporting continuous innovation and professional development.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

In this leadership role, you will guide a portfolio of programs, develop strong customer relationships, and empower teams to achieve operational and strategic objectives. Your responsibilities will include:

Provide leadership and strategic vision across a portfolio of programs, motivating teams to achieve program goals and broader organizational objectives.
Foster a culture of servant leadership, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Lead, mentor, and develop Program Managers, strengthening leadership capabilities and supporting talent management across the group.
Engage regularly with customer stakeholders to understand their priorities, maintain strong relationships, and ensure high levels of customer satisfaction.
Participate in program reviews, evaluate performance, identify areas for improvement, and mature program management processes when necessary.
Lead tactical and strategic planning activities to support program execution, portfolio performance, and organizational growth.
Maintain consistent communication with key customers and internal stakeholders, ensuring transparency and alignment.
Identify and pursue new business development opportunities, including capabilities briefings, contract growth, and program expansion.
Work with customers to identify capability gaps, understand requirements, and collaborate with technical teams to develop appropriate solutions.
Encourage innovation and proactively identify opportunities to improve services, capabilities, and customer outcomes.

Requirements

The ideal candidate brings extensive program management experience, strong leadership capabilities, and a customer-focused approach to strategic growth. Required qualifications include:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
At least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including a minimum of 10 years in traditional program management.
Demonstrated experience leading and mentoring multiple Program Managers.
Proven ability to establish and communicate a strategic vision while driving meaningful organizational change and growth.
Strong experience in customer-facing roles, gathering requirements, and collaborating with technical teams to develop solutions.
A track record of building strong customer relationships and maintaining high levels of customer satisfaction.
Demonstrated ability to build, engage, and empower leadership teams and established workforces, including talent development and management.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to foster collaboration, transparency, and open communication.
An entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to identify customer capability gaps and turn them into innovative opportunities.
Strong strategic planning, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

A Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is preferred.

Benefits

401(k) plan with a 6% company match and immediate vesting.
Highly subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Legal Resources Plan.
On-site gym facility.
Vacation leave and separate personal/sick leave.
10 paid federal holidays.
Company-paid life insurance.
Company-paid short-term and long-term disability coverage.
Flexible working hours and a casual work environment.
Remote work flexibility with a company-provided laptop, alongside the option to work from a renovated office.
Opportunities for professional growth through leadership development, training, conferences, and technical knowledge-sharing.
Peer-to-peer and on-the-job learning within a highly technical team.
Free refreshments and snacks.
Company-sponsored weekly breakfasts or lunches.
Holiday celebrations and family picnics.
Opportunities to participate in charitable and community events.

new_jobs.title: Regional Program Manager, Field Sales
new_jobs.description:
Archer
is collaborating with Barclays
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.

Join Barclays as a Regional Program Manager, Field Sales, where you will confidently interact with region, district, and store level management to ensure the success of our retail credit card partnerships. You will manage field execution of Barclays retail cobrand credit card program, drive credit card account acquisitions and usage in partner stores across the territory and develop productive relationships with partner field management.

To be successful as a Regional Program Manager, Field Sales, you should have experience with:

General relationship/business development/marketing/sales experience required
Success in influencing external partners as well as internal colleagues
Retail industry experience with general understanding of credit products

Some Other Highly Valued Skills May Include

Financial Services Retail Support Function OR Retail store/district/region management experience
Exercise ample oral and written communication skills
Ability to provide clear insights, effective coaching, and actionable feedback to partners and internal contacts in alignment with business objectives

You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for success in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.

We are open to candidates working from home based in Massachusetts.

Minimum Salary: $100,000

Maximum Salary: $145,000

The minimum and maximum salary/rate information above include only base salary or base hourly rate. It does not include any other type of compensation or benefits that may be available.

Purpose of the role

To develop, implement and manage marketing strategies through direct interactions with partners and their employees, including establishment of campaign budgets, monitoring of performance metrics, and implementation of data-driven optimisations to improve ROI

Accountabilities

Development and implementation of marketing strategies for face to face channels, including as applicable, bank branches, partner physical locations and other physical locations. This includes the identification of target audiences and establishment campaign objectives.
Management of marketing campaigns across face to face channels, including development of training materials, promotional materials, coordination with partners and their employees, and as applicable, branch staff, while ensuring compelling, consistent messaging across all customer touchpoints.
Analysis of campaign performance of face to face initiatives, and preparation of regular reports to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing campaigns.
Enhancement of the customer experience within face to face channels, to streamline processes, and optimise the physical environment to create a positive and engaging experience, as applicable.
Management of performance marketing budget for face to face channels, ensuring efficient allocation of resources, including monitoring of campaign costs, negotiation of contracts with vendors, and optimisation of spending to achieve marketing objectives.
Evaluation of market research (including voice of the customer and the partner employees) and competitive analysis to identify industry trends, consumer behaviour, and competitive positioning within face to face channels.

Assistant Vice President Expectations

To advise and influence decision making, contribute to policy development and take responsibility for operational effectiveness. Collaborate closely with other functions/ business divisions.
Lead a team performing complex tasks, using well developed professional knowledge and skills to deliver on work that impacts the whole business function. Set objectives and coach employees in pursuit of those objectives, appraisal of performance relative to objectives and determination of reward outcomes
If the position has leadership responsibilities, People Leaders are expected to demonstrate a clear set of leadership behaviours to create an environment for colleagues to thrive and deliver to a consistently excellent standard. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others.
OR for an individual contributor, they will lead collaborative assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will identify new directions for assignments and/ or projects, identifying a combination of cross functional methodologies or practices to meet required outcomes.
Consult on complex issues; providing advice to People Leaders to support the resolution of escalated issues.
Identify ways to mitigate risk and developing new policies/procedures in support of the control and governance agenda.
Take ownership for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work done.
Perform work that is closely related to that of other areas, which requires understanding of how areas coordinate and contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the organisation sub-function.
Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategy.
Engage in complex analysis of data from multiple sources of information, internal and external sources such as procedures and practises (in other areas, teams, companies, etc).to solve problems creatively and effectively.
Communicate complex information. 'Complex' information could include sensitive information or information that is difficult to communicate because of its content or its audience.
Influence or convince stakeholders to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager/Solution Delivery Specialist, Enterprise Systems
new_jobs.description:
Location:
New York, NY Category:
Staff Job Type:
Full-time Posted On:
Fri Oct 23 2026 Job Description:

Reporting to the Executive Director, IT Administration & Solution Delivery Center, this position provides comprehensive project management, process improvement, business analysis, business relationship management, and information systems administration for IT Division's enterprise systems and services as assigned. The position manages projects from concept through implementation and completion using both waterfall and agile methodologies.

The position serves as a business analyst and systems administrator for assigned functional areas and systems, developing a strong understanding of the supported units' business processes, operational needs, and technology requirements. Responsibilities include developing business and technical requirements; designing and building reports; supporting the requirements and design of queries, APIs, and system interfaces; performing and coordinating system testing and configuration; troubleshooting and resolving system issues; and serving as a liaison between IT and supported business units.

The position typically leads or participates as a member of cross-functional project teams and may also work independently as an individual contributor on assigned projects and initiatives. The role requires the ability to manage multiple priorities, collaborate with stakeholders across the organization, and provide timely and effective support for enterprise systems and services. Occasional evening and weekend work, overtime, and response to enterprise application outages or escalations may be required based on project and operational support needs.

Essential Functions

Project Management and Process Improvement

Act as lead project and process manager for your assigned customers and units.
Deliver projects on-time, on-budget, and in scope.
Plan and develop an accurate project portfolio in relation to the IT roadmap with leadership oversight and guidance.
Manage project schedules, budget, resources, communications, issues, risks, status reports, and implementation.
Work to improve business processes by mapping as is and future state maps and develop solutions.
Provide project and process support for the design, development, configuration, customization, and implementation of third-party and custom applications, systems, and services.
Manage and administer assigned systems and services, using appropriate business, analysis, and development tools.

Business Analysis and Business Relationship Management

Translate business needs into functional and technical requirements.
Perform documentation and business/technical analysis associated with system maintenance, modifications, and enhancements.
Design and author requirements, configurations, and specifications for systems/services, working closely with enterprise software engineers.
Document, coordinate, and participate in designing/planning/scheduling and UAT testing and system implementation.
Review new systems, modules, workflows for potential implementation.
Knowledge-share new and enhanced technologies to stakeholders.
Provide timely, responsive, and effective service to assigned customers and units.
Liaise with vendors and interact in a highly-paced and collaborative environment.

IT and Enterprise Systems Support

Provide device and system knowledge, and leadership for design, development, maintenance, and support of IT and higher education systems.
Manage and administer assigned systems and services, using appropriate business, analysis, and development tools.
Develop and facilitate complex reports using Argos and other business intelligence, analysis, and development tools.

Collaboration

Collaborate with the manager on unit goals and execute strategic initiatives as directed.
Communicate and collaborate with stakeholders for daily operations and to deliver/promote unit services/initiatives/projects.

Training

Oversee customer training programs within your assigned customers and units.
Collaborate with the IT Training Unit for logistics and administrative support during training periods.
Train FIT employees, with vendor assistance as needed, on applications, systems, and/or tools related to the unit's supported operations.

Documentation

Develop documentation (charters, implementation plans, user guides, knowledge based articles, etc.) for existing, modified, and/or new systems and services.

The preceding description is not designed to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities required of the position; other duties may be assigned consistent with the classification of the position.

Job Requirements

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
5 years of professional experience in project management, business analysis, information systems, or a related technology field involving the analysis, documentation, design, and delivery of technology services.
Experience managing technology projects and priorities and working with business stakeholders to identify and address technology needs.
Experience with process improvement, systems implementation, testing, or technical support.
Experience troubleshooting technical issues and working collaboratively with IT and business teams.
Strong written, verbal, analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a higher education IT environment.
Experience supporting or administering enterprise systems.
Experience developing custom reports, business intelligence solutions, automated workflows, or related data solutions.
Experience with project management methodologies and/or Agile practices.
PMP or Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) certification.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Knowledge of project management, business analysis, process management, and technology implementation practices.
Knowledge of enterprise applications, systems administration, and technology-supported business operations.
Strong analytical, critical-thinking, troubleshooting, and complex problem-solving skills.
Ability to translate business needs into clear technical and functional requirements.
Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines in a collaborative environment.
Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong interpersonal, organizational, documentation, and customer-service skills.
Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively to cross-functional project teams.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Microsoft Project; familiarity with Google Workspace and reporting/query tools.

Additional Information

Please note all offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of the background check process.

CBA Title

Project Manager

Salary

Salary: $99,777.63 - $144,170.54 per year commensurate with experience and qualifications.

The UCE-FIT Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) dictates the compensation, benefits, and conditions of employment. Hiring Salary: $99,777.63 per year with step increments per Salary Schedule 96, after one year of service and annually thereafter.

Work Schedule

Days/Hours: M-F, 9am-5pm, in person; work schedule subject to change based on needs of the department.

Benefits

The Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) provides comprehensive employee benefit programs designed to help keep our faculty and staff and their families healthy, safe, happy, and productive. Our programs also include a variety of components to help our employees improve the quality and balance of their work and family lives, and to help them prepare for their futures.

Retirement Plans

Health Care Plan and Dental Plan
Employee Assistance Program
Flexible Spending Account
Commuter Benefit Plan
FIT Tuition Exemption Program
Paid Time Off (Vacation, Personal, Sick and Holidays)
4-day Summer Workweek
Qualifying Employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program

For a full list of FIT benefits, visit our benefits webpage.

Pay Equity by State Employers

Pursuant to Executive Order 161, no State entity, as defined by the Executive Order, is permitted to ask, or mandate, in any form, that an applicant for employment provide his or her current compensation, or any prior compensation history, until such time as the applicant is extended a conditional offer of employment with compensation. If such information has been requested from you before such time, please contact the Governor's Office of Employee Relations at (518) 474-6988 or via email at info@goer.ny.gov.

Visa Sponsorship

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship by the Fashion Institute of Technology.

FIT is firmly committed to creating an environment that will attract and retain people from a range of backgrounds. FIT is committed to providing equal opportunity in employment, including the opportunity for upward mobility for all qualified individuals. Applications from veterans and persons with disabilities are encouraged. Inquiries regarding FIT's non-discrimination policies may be directed to the Chief Equal Employment Opportunity Officer/Title IX Coordinator, 212 217.3360.

The safety and well-being of FIT's students, faculty, staff, and visitors is of paramount importance. A paper copy of the report will be provided upon request by contacting Public Safety's administrative office number at (212) 217-4999.

new_jobs.title: Education Program Manager, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

The best leaders don't measure success by what they accomplish themselves. They measure it by what the people around them achieve.

If you've managed programs, built high-performing teams, and held people accountable to ambitious goals, this role offers the chance to apply those skills where they'll shape the next generation.

At Alpha, students don't spend their days listening to lectures. They master academics through adaptive technology while Guides focus on coaching, motivation, accountability, and life skills. As a Lead Guide, you'll run the program that makes this model work—managing the people, the operations, and the outcomes, from coaching Guides to developing leaders to creating an environment where students consistently exceed expectations.

This is not an instructional coaching role, and it is not classroom teaching. You won't spend your days reviewing lesson plans or observing lectures because there aren't any. Instead, you'll build a culture of excellence by coaching Guides, leading engaging life skills workshops, and motivating students to achieve ambitious goals. Your success will be measured by the quality of students' experiences, your team's performance, and your ability to maintain uncompromising standards while inspiring others to meet them.

Alpha is building the world's best K-12 experience. That requires leaders who have already proven they can raise others' performance, make objective, data-driven decisions, and embrace bold new ideas rather than protecting outdated traditions. If that describes you, we'd love to meet you.

This role is currently open at select Alpha campuses: Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; New York City, NY; Greenwich, CT; and Washington, DC.

If you're located in one of these markets—or excited to relocate—we'd love to hear from you. Exceptional candidates outside these locations are also encouraged to apply. As Alpha continues to grow, we regularly match outstanding leaders with opportunities across our expanding network of campuses.

What You Will Be Doing

Coaching Guides to consistently deliver exceptional student experiences while maintaining Alpha's high standards.
Leading engaging life skills workshops that develop communication, leadership, focus, and other real-world skills for K-12 students.
Motivating students to achieve ambitious learning goals and maximize progress in their self-directed academic programs.
Using data, observation, and coaching conversations to improve Guide performance and student outcomes.
Helping launch and establish new Alpha campuses by building a culture centered on excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching traditional academic classes or delivering subject-matter lectures.
Writing lesson plans or designing curriculum.
Lowering standards to make students feel successful instead of helping them achieve real mastery.
Managing a team from behind a desk without regularly coaching students and Guides firsthand.
Preserving outdated practices simply because "that's how we've always done it."

Education Program Manager Key Responsibilities

Ensure every student consistently experiences Alpha's three promises by building high-performing Guides, delivering engaging life skills experiences, and maintaining uncompromising standards for student success.

Basic Requirements

Willingness to work on-site at an Alpha campus (relocation support available): Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; New York City, NY; Greenwich, CT; Washington, DC
Bachelor's degree in Education, Psychology, Business, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.
At least 5 years of experience in education, coaching, learning and development, or a related leadership role.
Experience leading and developing teams of five or more people, including hiring and making performance-based termination decisions.
Demonstrated success using data to drive performance improvements.
Experience working with children ages 5-14 in an educational, coaching, or developmental setting.
Experience building or launching a new team, program, business, school, or initiative, with willingness to help open a new campus from zero.
Willingness to work in a school model that rejects traditional lecture-based pedagogy.
Legal authorization to work in the United States.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience coaching youth through athletics, debate, camps, or extracurricular programs.
Exceptional public speaking and storytelling skills.
A track record of achieving high levels of academic, professional, or athletic performance.
Experience motivating teams through ambitious goals while maintaining high accountability.
A passion for challenging conventional education and helping shape a new model for K-12 learning.

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $200,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.
